greeting: Good morning, Zuhair. Grab a coffee, it's a big Saturday of news.

lead.headline: Police widen Operation Phoenix across Melbourne's suburbs
lead.summary: Victoria Police is expanding its arson and extortion taskforce from the north-west into the CBD and south-east, folding in resources from Operation Trinity. The operation has already led to hundreds of arrests amid continuing firebombings.

stories.headline: Fractal basins may explain why deep learning is hard to reproduce
stories.summary: Published in Nature Machine Intelligence this week, the paper argues that the regions of parameter space leading to different training outcomes are intertwined like a fractal, so even tiny changes in initialisation can flip the result. It is drawing attention as an explanation for irreproducibility in deep learning.

stories.headline: New dataset and benchmark for predicting T cell receptor binding
stories.summary: A Nature Computational Science resource paper introduces Hi-TPH, a large hierarchical dataset, and protein language models fine-tuned on it to predict how T cell receptors bind peptide-HLA complexes. It also shows how different molecular components contribute to prediction accuracy.

stories.headline: Thinking Machines Lab reportedly raising billions at a $40B valuation
stories.summary: Mira Murati's startup is said to be in talks for a round of roughly $5-6 billion led by Accel, with Nvidia possibly contributing around $2.5 billion. The deal has not been confirmed or closed.

stories.headline: OpenAI says an unreleased cyber model found hundreds of Linux privilege-escalation flaws
stories.summary: A write-up of OpenAI's report says an AI-led pipeline reproduced thousands of issues and grouped working variants into 948 candidate patches. The exact figure is secondhand and its model is not yet available.

stories.headline: AI news roundup: new US Justice Department task force on AI misuse
stories.summary: The daily roundup notes a Justice Department unit set up to investigate unlawful uses of advanced AI, alongside other industry developments from 6 November.

stories.headline: Food delivery rider killed in Melbourne CBD stabbing
stories.summary: Police say a rider was fatally stabbed near Queen Victoria Market after confronting a man allegedly tampering with bikes. A man has been arrested.

stories.headline: Three injured in stabbing at Dandenong home
stories.summary: A woman and two men were hurt in Melbourne's south-east, and police say those involved knew each other and no one else is being sought.

stories.headline: Nurse allegedly sexually assaulted at Thomas Embling Hospital
stories.summary: Police are investigating the alleged attack by a patient, while WorkSafe is making inquiries about staff safety concerns.

stories.headline: Retailers watch jerry can purchases as firebombings continue
stories.summary: Police have teamed up with shops to flag suspicious fuel and jerry can purchases following repeated firebombings across the city.

stories.headline: Trump says US will end $4 billion annual military aid to Israel
stories.summary: In an Election Day interview, Trump said he had agreed with Israel to stop the aid, while arms sales would continue. Reports differ on timing and the existing agreement runs to 2028.

stories.headline: Bomb threats disrupt flights across Europe
stories.summary: Several flights were diverted or searched after bomb threats, but no explosive devices were found and nobody has claimed responsibility.

thought: Small differences in the starting point can change the whole outcome.
